items.title: EES-WWO-25-002, 2024 Drinking Water Summary Report
notes:
Jennifer Rose, Commissioner, Engineering and Environmental Services, introduced the report and provided a presentation. She noted that it speaks to the details of the water system in the Region and the associated supply metrics. In addition, she elaborated on the Standard of Care and inspections that the municipality is required to uphold and carry out.

In response to a question from the Committee, J. Rose indicated that water and asset management may be affected by the implementation and tariffs, including through valve replacement.

In reply to a question from the Committee, J. Rose spoke to the growth patterns and expectations in the Region as they pertain to the effects of climate change and water/wastewater supply and maintenance. She indicated that staff has been given direction to look within the Regional borders to locate more water sources to support growth. Furthermore, staff are looking at capacity as it relates to big storms occurring as a result of climate change, which can impact pipes and flooding.

Responding to a question from the Committee, J. Rose reassured that all options for water preservation are being explored, including grey water strategies.

items.title: PDL-LEG-25-011, Authorization to Expropriate Lands (1st Report) for Improvements to Lancaster Street West (Phase 1), in the City of Kitchener
notes:
Fiona McCrea, Acting Regional Solicitor and Director of Legal Services, spoke to the report.

Replying to a question from the Committee, F. McCrea clarified that expropriation reports are brought forward in anticipation of initiating proceedings as needed. Thus, to ensure the land is in possession when work needs to commence which is consistent with other projects. Furthermore, J. Rose spoke to the construction timeline and added that land acquisition is also done with consideration to relocate utilities. F. McCrea also discussed that work could be delayed if the expropriation tool was not available at the time.

In response to a question from the Committee, J. Rose clarified that this is the first step in the standard land acquisition process, and that discussions are in place with property owners, with the intent being to avoid expropriation. She provided that the entire process, including negotiations, could take 18 months. F. McCrea added that the wording, format, and the report itself is the standard outline.

motions.item_title: PDL-LEG-25-012, Authorization to Expropriate Lands (2nd Report) for Replacement of the Scheifele Bridge on Northfield Drive East (Regional Road 22), in the Township of Woolwich
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the expropriation of the following lands for the proposed replacement of the Scheifele Bridge on Northfield Drive East (Regional Road 22), in the Township of Woolwich, in the Regional Municipality of Waterloo, as detailed in report PDL-LEG-25-012, dated March 4, 2025: Fee Simple Partial Taking: Part of Lot 32, German Company Tract, being Parts 1, 3 & 4 on 58R-22126, Township of Woolwich, Part of PIN 22705-0403 (LT) (698 Northfield Drive, Waterloo). Temporary Easement: The right and easement, being a temporary easement in gross, for the free and unobstructed, right, interest and easement terminating, for the subject properties set out below, on the 31st day of December, 2028, for itself, its successors and assigns, and anyone authorized by it, on, over, under and through the following properties for the purpose of stock piling of materials and/or equipment as required in connection with the adjacent construction, and all related improvements, and works ancillary thereto and for such purposes, the free, unimpeded and unobstructed access to the lands at all times by employees, agents, contractors, workers and anyone authorized by it, and vehicles, supplies and equipment at all times and for all purposes and things necessary for or incidental to the exercise and enjoyment of the right and easement: Part of Lot 32, German Company Tract, being Part 2 on 58R-22126, Township of Woolwich, Part of PIN 22705-0403 (LT) (698 Northfield Drive, Waterloo); Part of Lot 3, German Company Tract, being Part 6 on 58R-22126, Township of Woolwich, Part of PIN 22705-0091 (LT)) (535 Northfield Drive, Waterloo). And that staff be instructed to register a Plan of Expropriation for the properties within three months of the granting of the approval to expropriate the properties, as required by the Expropriations Act; And that the registered owners be served with a Notice of Expropriation and a Notice of Possession for the properties after the registration of the Plan of Expropriation and the Regional Solicitor is authorized to take any and all actions required to enforce such Notices including but not limited to any application pursuant to Section 40 of the Expropriations Act; And that the Regional Solicitor is authorized to enter into an agreement with the registered owners, or to make an application under Section 39 of the Expropriations Act, to adjust the date for possession specified in the Notice of Possession as may be required; And that all above-referenced fee simple partial takings situated adjacent to an existing Regional public highway be acquired for road widening purposes and therefore be deemed to form part of the adjacent public highway in accordance with subsection 31(6) of the Municipal Act, 2001 ; And that if no agreement as to compensation is made with an owner, the statutory Offer of Compensation and payment be served upon the registered owners of the properties in the amount of the market value of the interests in the land as estimated by the Region’s appraiser in accordance with the Expropriations Act ; And that the Regional Solicitor be authorized to execute any Indemnity agreement or other document related to payment of the statutory Offer of Compensation; And further that the Regional Solicitor be authorized to discontinue expropriation proceedings or any part thereof, in respect of the above described lands, or any part thereof, upon the registration on title of the required documentation to complete the transaction or if determined by the Commissioner, Engineering & Environmental Services, that such lands, or any part or interest thereof, are not required for the subject Project.
